Purpose and principal workflow

acme.sh is a dependency-light shell ACME client for issuing, renewing, and installing TLS certificates. The workflow starts either when a human operator invokes the CLI or when the installed cron scheduler runs the daily renewal command; the client performs ACME validation, stores certificate artifacts, optionally installs them into a service, and can notify an operator.

Components

Entry and lifecycle

  • Command/lifecycle CLI — acme.sh: Handles commands such as --install, issuance, renewal, certificate installation, and --cron; the README documents these entry points and the installer’s cron setup.
  • Human operator — null repository path: Initiates interactive installation, issuance, renewal, or installation commands.
  • Installed cron scheduler — null repository path: Generates the documented daily --cron invocation after installation.
  • Certificate home/state — null repository path; runtime location documented as ~/.acme.sh: Holds the installed client and certificate files according to the installation guide.

ACME issuance and validation

  • ACME protocol/challenge engine — acme.sh: Implements the RFC 8555 client workflow and supports webroot, standalone, TLS-ALPN, Apache, Nginx, DNS, alias, stateless, and persistent-DNS validation modes.
  • ACME certificate authority — null repository path: External ACME endpoint; documented options include ZeroSSL as the default, Let’s Encrypt, SSL.com, Google Public CA, Actalis, Pebble, and other RFC 8555 authorities.
  • DNS challenge adapters — dnsapi: Provides provider-specific DNS integration scripts for DNS-based validation; the large catalog and the README’s DNS mode establish this as a distinct integration surface.
  • DNS provider — null repository path: External authoritative DNS service whose TXT records can satisfy DNS-01 challenges.
  • HTTP/TLS challenge surface — null repository path: Existing web servers or the client’s standalone listeners used for HTTP-01 and TLS-ALPN validation.

Post-issuance integrations

  • Certificate deployment adapters — deploy: Contains integrations for installing or updating certificates in servers, appliances, control panels, and other target systems.
  • Certificate-consuming service — null repository path: External web server, appliance, or application that receives the renewed certificate.
  • Notification adapters — notify: Contains notification integrations for renewal and error events, matching the README’s cron-notification feature.
  • Notification endpoint — null repository path: External mail, chat, paging, or webhook service receiving notifications.

Relationships

  • Human operator -> Command/lifecycle CLI: invokes installation, issuance, renewal, or installation commands; documented usage is command-line based.
  • Installed cron scheduler -> Command/lifecycle CLI: invokes the daily --cron renewal check; specified by the installer documentation.
  • Command/lifecycle CLI -> ACME protocol/challenge engine: dispatches lifecycle commands into issuance, renewal, and validation operations within the shell client.
  • ACME protocol/challenge engine -> ACME certificate authority: sends ACME protocol requests for authorization, issuance, and renewal.
  • ACME certificate authority -> ACME protocol/challenge engine: returns ACME authorization and certificate responses.
  • ACME protocol/challenge engine -> DNS challenge adapters: selects DNS-mode integrations when DNS validation is requested; exact dynamic dispatch is not visible in the sample.
  • DNS challenge adapters -> DNS provider: perform provider-specific DNS challenge operations; the adapter catalog establishes the interface, although individual call sites were not sampled.
  • ACME protocol/challenge engine -> HTTP/TLS challenge surface: uses the selected webroot, Apache, Nginx, standalone, or TLS-ALPN validation mode.
  • Command/lifecycle CLI -> Certificate home/state: creates or renews certificate artifacts in the documented client home.
  • Command/lifecycle CLI -> Certificate deployment adapters: optionally passes issued or renewed certificates to the selected installation integration.
  • Certificate deployment adapters -> Certificate-consuming service: installs certificate material into the target service; exact adapter sequencing is not shown.
  • Command/lifecycle CLI -> Notification adapters: emits renewal or error events for configured notifications.
  • Notification adapters -> Notification endpoint: delivers those events through the selected external notification channel.

Coverage limits

No source excerpts were provided. The repository tree and README establish the product boundaries and documented modes, but not function-level call order, certificate/state formats, adapter dispatch mechanics, or the precise behavior of each provider and deployment script.
